topics.question_text: One source writes: "Use the stable package facade and a simple generated series.". Think of a recent case where you had to judge whether something was stable package. Describe one case that clearly was, one that clearly was not, and one that was hard to call. What differed between them, and what did you check first?

"PCMCI-AMI orchestration now follows the inward-only dependency rule: use cases depend on declared ports (protocol contracts), and adapters satisfy those contracts without adapter-to-adapter helper coupling.". Describe a case where this did not hold, or where you decided against it. What about that case told you it was an exception?

"Use cases orchestrate triage models, pipeline helpers, and internal services, and depend on causal discovery through declared `ports/` contracts.". Describe a case where this did not hold, or where you decided against it. What about that case told you it was an exception?

Sources prescribe: "Without BH FDR correction when many drivers are tested simultaneously: uncorrected $p$-values will inflate false-positive rates.". Think of the last time you did this. What result did you get, what had you expected, what did that result make you do next -- and what result would have sent you down a different path?

Sources prescribe: "As a sole decision-maker: F6 is a complementary contextual tool, not a forecastability measure.". Think of the last time you did this. What result did you get, what had you expected, what did that result make you do next -- and what result would have sent you down a different path?

Sources prescribe: "Start with forecastability triage first: readiness, leakage risk, informative horizons, primary lags, seasonality structure, and covariate informativeness.". Think of the last time you did this. What result did you get, what had you expected, what did that result make you do next -- and what result would have sent you down a different path?

Sources prescribe: "significance counts are currently zero across this canonical summary (`n_sig_ami=0`, `n_sig_pami=0` for all 8), so actionable lag decisions should rely on class-level screening plus domain checks rather than significance-lag selection alone.". Think of the last time you did this. What result did you get, what had you expected, what did that result make you do next -- and what result would have sent you down a different path?

Sources prescribe: "Which model families are plausible enough to test next?". Think of the last time you did this. What result did you get, what had you expected, what did that result make you do next -- and what result would have sent you down a different path?

Sources prescribe: "When you need a principled multiple-testing correction to control false positives across many candidate drivers.". Think of the last time you did this. What result did you get, what had you expected, what did that result make you do next -- and what result would have sent you down a different path?

"When selecting the lookback window for a forecasting model: use the recommended plateau $k^*$ as a principled starting point.". Think of the last time you made this choice. Which options did you consider, which did you take, and what about that situation decided it? When did you last choose differently?

"When screening a large panel of candidate series to prioritise modelling effort.". Think of the last time you made this choice. Which options did you consider, which did you take, and what about that situation decided it? When did you last choose differently?

"When candidate exogenous variables are available and you need to decide which, if any, are worth including in a multivariate model.". Think of the last time you made this choice. Which options did you consider, which did you take, and what about that situation decided it? When did you last choose differently?

"For short series ($n < 128$): Welch PSD estimates are based on very few segments and Ω values are unreliable as anything other than a coarse indicator.". Think of the last time you made this choice. Which options did you consider, which did you take, and what about that situation decided it? When did you last choose differently?

"Is there a seasonal structure worth modeling?". Think of the last time you made this choice. Which options did you consider, which did you take, and what about that situation decided it? When did you last choose differently?
